nodes.summary: The chosen gradient tower preserves loop information, with exact support costs for revision and a replication cost multiplier. Native edits add finite-grid choices; endogenous control and representation-independent dimensional continuity remain open. Execution is paused for the agreed issues.

nodes.title: Exact dimensional compatibility without guard rows
nodes.summary: Literal replication intertwines every adjacent axial dimension for exactly 66 ECA sources. This removes guards while retaining a prepared replication code, source word in the law, and processing that grows with dimension.

nodes.title: Dimensional compatibility and axis order are separate constraints
nodes.summary: Exactly 24 ECA sources commute across spatial axes and 14 also preserve replication. Another 52 preserve the beam with ordered axes. The classification concerns this constructor and axis permutations, not reflections.

nodes.title: Do transverse differences evolve autonomously?
nodes.summary: The unchanged 66-source experiment finds six autonomous transverse laws and sixty full-field obstructions. A separately frozen witness-extension audit resolves three failures hidden by the original 3-by-3 periodic control.

nodes.title: Rule, state family, and interpretation form an explicit contract
nodes.summary: Truth-table addresses and lattice addresses are distinct. Research claims must declare their interpreter, encoding, and causal resources, while separating preservation, faithful representation, restoration, and endogenous organization.

nodes.title: Transverse differences alone discard causally necessary column baselines
nodes.summary: Exactly six of the 66 compatible axial sources admit autonomous transverse-difference dynamics. For the other sixty, identical full observations have different next values, ruling out every deterministic update on that observation alone.

nodes.title: Does retaining both spatial differences restore closure?
nodes.summary: The unchanged 66-source comparison admits ten full-gradient laws, including four nonlinear majority variants. A complement-factor proof and complete-field certificates classify all 56 failures; image constraints and storage costs remain explicit.

nodes.title: Complement symmetry makes the full gradient autonomous
nodes.summary: Exactly ten of 66 compatible axial sources factor through the full gradient, including four nonlinear majority variants. A constant local complement response is necessary and sufficient; all 56 failures have complete-field witnesses.

nodes.title: Does loop information survive gradient evolution and dimensional lifting?
nodes.summary: Native gradient evolution and both dimensional interfaces agree with independent twisted-potential references. Eight self-dual sources preserve wrapping-loop bits; constants erase them. The invariant depends on explicit periodic topology.

nodes.title: Loop sectors persist under self-dual gradient dynamics
nodes.summary: Translation covariance and complement response give h'=kappa*h: eight self-dual sources conserve every periodic loop bit, while constants erase them. Replication appends zero; native 1D/2D/3D audits agree independently.

nodes.title: Can persistent loop information be affordably revised?
nodes.summary: The complete flat-mask audit proves minimum loop-changing support and replication cost, and counts inherited versus native usable futures. Independent endpoint checks agree; period-two bijectivity limits generalization. The external action interface is explicit.

nodes.title: Loop revision has a support cost; inherited control has a replication cost
nodes.summary: Changing loop vector h costs exactly the sum of transverse section sizes over changed directions. Replication multiplies both edge and site costs by the added period. Native actions add finite-grid outcomes under a declared external known-state interface.

nodes.title: Factor existence differs from candidate-law disagreement
nodes.summary: A factor is unique on the observed image when equal current observations have equal next observations. A nonzero candidate-law error can coexist with exact closure, as Rule255 shows.

nodes.title: Future equivalence is the minimal predictive refinement
nodes.summary: Observed-future partitions stabilize on finite systems at the coarsest invariant refinement of the observation. Finite closure does not imply bounded memory, locality or an online learning algorithm.

nodes.title: Hidden differences have observer- and context-dependent fates
nodes.summary: The finite observer census and Rule106 witnesses show that the same defect shape can be permanently hidden or later visible depending on its common context and observation.

nodes.title: Forgotten information splits into latent and shielded parts
nodes.summary: Under a declared prior, forgotten information splits into unresolved observed-future distinctions and distinctions absent from the complete observed future. This is separate from action-dependent control.

nodes.title: Breaking closure cheaply and maximizing hidden futures are different objectives
nodes.summary: For 222 of 247 ECA rules with a tested static closure breaker at n=12, no tested observer jointly optimizes minimum closure-breaking loss and maximum future repertoire.

nodes.title: Representation repair fixes the future target while refining the present
nodes.summary: The complete two-cell partition census finds globally optimal greedy repair in 1,590 nonclosed cases. Fixed target semantics, ensemble weighting and worst-case tails remain distinct.

nodes.title: A useful distinction can depend on distinctions already represented
nodes.summary: The block-three census has four exact greedy failures in 30,856 nonclosed cases. A zero-gain bridge can make a later distinction more valuable; this supplies no adaptive-policy optimum.

nodes.title: Ternary transport roles have an algebraic redundancy bound
nodes.summary: LR=RL and LC=CL bound distinct exact-depth roles by 2^(d+1)-1. The finite eight-cell role census and semantic lift do not establish autonomous physical lifting or retained-information growth.

nodes.title: Local product approximations lose successor correlations
nodes.summary: The reproduced Rule110/n=8 example compares exact full-field successor sets with sound local product sets; precision and probability conventions remain separate.

nodes.title: Which sound approximations preserve useful precision?
nodes.summary: Ordered approximation domains, resource costs and whole-field precision remain an open Program direction beyond the archived finite example.

nodes.title: Decoded rule-field transport is invariant under local relabeling
nodes.summary: Table conjugation, a decoded old-state gate and destination table conversion preserve the joint dynamics exactly; seeded checks remain separate.

nodes.title: What is the rule-field dimensional lift?
nodes.summary: The relabeling identity supplies an interpreter example; the proposed lift still needs an alphabet, decoder, update schedule and admissible family.

nodes.title: Constructor intersections retain their separate domains
nodes.summary: Saved-result extraction reports four scoped sets and all pairwise intersections, keeping the nonlinear gradient comparisons and finite/intrinsic role distinction visible.

nodes.title: Shared-family whole-field fibers are completion-independent
nodes.summary: The triangular coordinate theorem gives local invertible recodings at each fixed finite depth for completions agreeing on an invariant family, preserving whole-field fibers and factor existence.

nodes.title: Compare second-lift cap radii under two Rule32 completions
nodes.summary: A frozen GF(2)^2 protocol separates inherited-family cap costs from a full-ambient control. Implementation and primary evaluation remain unrun.

nodes.title: Compare future repertoire with representation empowerment
nodes.summary: The hidden-state no-op/flip census uses fixed observer/cadence pairs, exact channels and capacity certificates. Implementation and evaluation remain unrun.

nodes.title: Conservative suffix prediction with explicit abstention
nodes.summary: An implemented sequence instrument uses one global suffix depth, successor sets and frozen held-out prediction. Its history cost is explicit; it is not the forward future-equivalence relation.

nodes.title: Preserved, covariant, or changed: classifying a property relative to a transformation
nodes.summary: A property is preserved, covariant with a stated transport of its value, or changed, always relative to a declared transformation with declared costs.

nodes.title: Which re-interpretations of a represented dynamics are admissible, and what does each cost?
nodes.summary: The record uses several distinct transformations; none is a group and each needs declared transports and costs.

nodes.title: The commutator is complement-covariant exactly for self-dual rules
nodes.summary: Under complement conjugation the native commutator is covariant iff the rule is self-dual (16 rules), proved by the exhaustive five-cell local check; transporting the derivative as a state restores covariance for all 256. Reflection preserves the classification.

nodes.title: Complement conjugation shifts local-cap radii by a bounded amount
nodes.summary: Reflection preserves all 4,608 cap budgets. Under complement conjugation 696 K cells keep their minimum radius, 54 differ with both finite (4 exceed the frozen ≤h bound, all at h=0), 18 are censored at R ≤ 2; every censored cell has a cap at radius 3 and the shift is at most 2.

nodes.title: Regime labels are more stable under relabeling than the statistics behind them
nodes.summary: On the sampled sweep, labels agree 95% (reflection) and 94% (complement) between a pair and its image while raw statistics agree under 30%; commute pairs agree exactly; disagreements are not concentrated on the two boundaries the protocol named.

nodes.title: Audit six ECA claims against complement conjugation and reflection
nodes.summary: Frozen audit of existing claims under two declared transformations; five of six predictions held, the cap-radius bound failed.

nodes.title: Extend the cap census to R ≤ 6 on the cells that disagreed with their complements
nodes.summary: All four frozen predictions held: caps exist on both sides, the bound holds, shifts are 1 or 2.

nodes.title: O-coordinate caps are complement-invariant; K caps shift by at most two
nodes.summary: At R ≤ 4 over all rules the O cap table is identical under complement conjugation and K radii shift by 0, 1 or 2; no cap is created or destroyed.

nodes.title: Census of cap-radius shifts under complement conjugation
nodes.summary: All six frozen predictions held over 256 rules, K and O, h ≤ 2, R ≤ 4.

nodes.title: The 2-block recoding costs at most one unit of cap radius and usually none
nodes.summary: In block coordinates the minimum cap radius is unchanged in 665 of 674 decided cells and reduced by one in 9, at two stored bits per site; derivative, commutator and closure transport componentwise under both tested ambient completions.

nodes.title: The possibility-frontier census is covariant under complement and reflection
nodes.summary: The observer family is closed under input complement and reversal with preserved block alignment, so the census's scalar per-rule summaries are identical for a rule, its conjugate and its mirror, with optimal observers corresponding under an explicit permutation; a deduction from a finite check.

nodes.title: Audit the 2-block recoding against caps, derivative, commutator, closure, and the observer family
nodes.summary: B1–B3 held on the consistent-pair family and the observer-family closure part of B4 held; B4's literal-summary consequence and the declared ambient radius were corrected after review.

nodes.title: Neighbor-parity coarse-graining closes exactly on the constant-complement-response rules
nodes.summary: Rule 102 as an observation closes for exactly the 32 rules with constant complement response at rings 4 to 12, each with an elementary factor; the factor map pairs complement-conjugates; the other 224 rules need at most two steps of history on every ring (certified in the sixth unit), exactly eight of them needing the second step.

nodes.title: Audit neighbor-parity coarse-graining against closure, the factor, the commutator, and the refinement chain
nodes.summary: Five frozen predictions held after gate-1 review; one dated implementation deviation at the JSON write.

nodes.title: Certify the history bound under neighbor-parity coarse-graining
nodes.summary: Finite 8-word certificate plus lemma proves h_* ≤ 2 on every ring for all rules; depth-2 set is exactly eight rules; exhaustive rings 7, 9, 11, 14 agree; run authorized before other-model review, which arrived retrospectively.

nodes.title: Closure under a linear observation is decided by its kernel; larger kernels keep only the affine rules
nodes.summary: Complement-pair kernels (60, 102, 90 on odd rings) reproduce the parity results; rule 90 on even rings and rule 150 on rings divisible by 3 close only the 16 affine rules; depth under those kernels reaches 4 within ring 12 and varies with ring size.

nodes.title: Audit all eight linear rules as observations: closure, kernel dependence, and history depth
nodes.summary: Seven frozen predictions held after gate-1 review; the exact closed sets under the richer kernels (the affine rules) were unpredicted.

nodes.title: Under block majority a rule closes by commuting with the observation or by collapsing it
nodes.summary: Exactly 22 rules close under majority on rings 6 to 12: 14 exact commuters with rule 232 and 8 whose observed successor is constant; the affine rules beyond constants, identity, shifts and complements do not close; depth reaches 16 at ring 12 and grows with the ring.

nodes.title: Audit block majority as an observation: closure, commutation, factor locality, and history depth
nodes.summary: All frozen predictions held after gate-1 review; the 22-rule closed set, the 14 commuters and the 8 collapse rules were reported, not predicted.

nodes.title: Under a non-linear observation, a rule can close with a factor that is neither constant nor the rule itself
nodes.summary: Under isolated-cell detection exactly 33 rules close on rings 6 to 12: 9 commuters, 24 collapse rules, and rules 123 and 251 with a non-constant factor that is not the rule; 251 is the complement of the observation, 123 only shares its observed successor on the tested rings. The frozen commute-or-collapse prediction failed, and complement conjugation is covariant only when the observation travels with the rule.

nodes.title: Audit isolated-cell detection as an observation: closure, commutation, collapse, factor locality, and history depth
nodes.summary: Six frozen predictions held after gate-1 review; the frozen commute-or-collapse prediction failed on rules 123 and 251; the 33-rule closed set and the depth census were reported.

nodes.title: The complement of an observation always closes; for rules 32, 200 and 22 it lies in the residual class
nodes.summary: The complement rule closes under every observation by construction. For observations 32, 200 and 22 it also lies in the residual class, but that class is not its equivalence class: under 32 every residual rule is equivalent to a commuter, under 200 none is and 16 factors are not elementary on the image, under 22 the closed set depends on the ring. Residual membership is not implied by non-self-duality. Observational equivalence is decided by five-cell words, certifying the rule-123 identity for every ring; majority's record depth reaches 31 at ring 16.

nodes.title: Audit the complement of the observation under rules 32, 200 and 22, with an observational-equivalence census and a depth annex
nodes.summary: Six frozen predictions held, including the depth annex bet; the frozen prediction that the residual class lies in the complement rule's equivalence class failed for rules 32 and 200 and at ring 6 for rule 22.
